definitions.explanation: Doing something without thinking; an action done despite not intending to.

examples.japanese: つい⟦{笑|わら}って→笑う：00685_warau⟧⟦しまった→仕舞う：03064_shimau⟧。
つい⟦{食|た}べ→食べる：00396_taberu⟧⟦{過|す}ぎて→過ぎる：01219_sugiru⟧⟦しまった→仕舞う：03064_shimau⟧。

examples.english: I inadvertently spoke my true feelings.

examples.english: I thought I had just come to Japan, but I was surprised that three years had already passed.

notes:
つい expresses actions done without intending to, often with a nuance of regret or lack of self-control.

POSITION IN SENTENCE:
- Usually appears at the beginning of a clause, before the verb

COMMON PATTERNS:
- つい〜て⟦しまう→仕舞う：03064_shimau⟧ (end up doing ~ unintentionally)
- つい⟦{先|さき}ほど→先程：04165_sakihodo⟧ (just a moment ago)
- つい⟦{最近|さいきん}→最近：00881_saikin⟧ (just recently)

USAGE:
- Implies the action was not fully intentional
- Often paired with て⟦しまう→仕舞う：03064_shimau⟧ to emphasize accidental nature
- Can express mild regret or excuse

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦うっかり→うっかり：01863_ukkari⟧: carelessly, by mistake (more accidental)
- ⟦{思|おも}わず→思わず：02549_omowazu⟧: involuntarily, without thinking (physical reflex)
